attrs.management_says: CFO increased due to changes in working capital and higher non-cash expenses (stock-based compensation, restructuring, inventory provisions), partially offset by lower net income.
attrs.numbers_show: Net income fell $16.6M ($630.6M → $614.0M) while CFO rose $269.3M ($905.7M → $1,175.0M). Inventory provisions charged to cost of sales rose $53M ($59M → $112M). SGA increased $121.2M ($480.8M → $602.0M), consistent with higher stock-based compensation. Restructuring charges are noted. The non-cash charge increase alone accounts for a large share of the CFO/net income gap.

attrs.reason: While inventory provisions rose $53M (E43) and SGA increased $121M (E3 vs E15), the pack does not disclose stock-based compensation expense, restructuring charges, or working capital changes (receivables, inventory, payables) needed to verify that these drivers are large enough to explain the $269M CFO increase alongside a $17M net income decline. The explanation relies on management's word (E48) for the working capital component.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The $269M CFO increase despite a $17M net income decline is largely explained by higher non-cash charges: inventory provisions rose $53M (from $59M to $112M), SGA increased $121M (partly reflecting stock-based compensation), and restructuring charges were incurred; these non-cash items reduce net income but are added back to CFO, while working capital changes also contributed per management.
